themes.theme: bond market repricing and yield pressure
themes.consensus_view: Bond yields have surged to multi-decade highs because traders are betting the Fed keeps raising rates, and while most banks expect that pressure to continue, a minority argue the market has priced in too many future hikes and yields should ease back.

facts_agreed.claim: The bond selloff is being driven by real yields and a hawkish repricing of Fed expectations, not by inflation fears.
evidence_quotes: pretty much all the move being driven by real yields.
Today's bond selloff is more about real-rate repricing and weak duration demand
the move is still primarily driven by a sharp repricing of the Fed.

facts_agreed.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield has broken out of its multi-year range to fresh highs and the uptrend is intact.
evidence_quotes: The 10-year has broken out of a three-year range
The uptrend remains intact unless the support levels at 4.75%, 4.67% and 4.54% are broken.

facts_agreed.claim: Rates volatility is elevated and is now spilling over into how other markets trade.
evidence_quotes: MOVE has exploded over the past two sessions.
Rates vol at current levels of c.90pts is not supportive for flows into riskier assets

facts_contested.claim: whether the market is overpricing the pace of further Fed rate hikes
facts_contested.for_evidence: we think they are overpricing what the Fed will deliver
facts_contested.against_evidence: The September increase is likely to be the first step in a longer cycle

facts_contested.claim: whether the bond selloff has overshot fair value and duration should be bought, or whether the drivers behind higher yields are still intact
facts_contested.for_evidence: we see merit in owning duration
facts_contested.against_evidence: The bearish narrative remains intact with none of the key drivers behind the recent sell-off
